correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs every scalar hypothesis and both subalgebra dimensions. The square-zero/idempotent equations prove the one-dimensional list. For planes P=ker(ell), the diagonal quadratic form ell(x²) is polarized in odd characteristic, and a rank-three nondegenerate form cannot have an isotropic plane. Rank-two radical geometry yields only the exceptional T at lambda=4. Explicit intersections prove the Boolean lattice and Frattini assertions, with Ku verified to be an ideal. The independently implemented exact finite-field enumeration covers all 22 nonzero parameters over p=3,5,7,11; no finite result is used as a universal proof.
